channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: In a Major Boost for the Right, Another Bolsonaro Nears Brazil’s Presidency
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s first round lead leaves President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva three weeks to find the votes to stop Brazil’s, and Latin America’s, rightward shift.

item.title: NPR: The iconic Arthur Read made his TV debut 30 years ago
item.description: The animated series "Arthur" premiered on PBS Kids on Oct. 7, 1996.

item.title: BBC News: King's funding for Andrew not to be used for legal action against police
item.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking action over search warrants issued ahead of his arrest in February.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘I spat in Sean Connery’s face 16 times’: Ron Perlman on making The Name of the Rose
item.description: ‘When I couldn’t do the spitting scene, Sean took me aside and said: “Ron, if you don’t actually spit in my face, we’ll be here all day.” So I let one fly – and kept having to redo it’ I read an article about a curious b…

item.title: Al Jazeera: UK ‘threatens to expel 27 Israeli diplomats’ over Jerusalem consulate
item.description: Israel ordered East Jerusalem consulate to be closed after Britain sanctioned settlements in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: Ars Technica: F1 in Bahrain... in Malaysia: The race needed a software update to start
item.description: A software bug waylaid half the field and required a race reboot.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Experience What It’s Like to Travel in the Occupied West Bank
item.description: Traverse barriers and checkpoints in the occupied West Bank—your choices reflect the reality of nearly 3.5 million Palestinians who live there.

item.title: WIRED Science: Astronomers Confirm Discovery of the Youngest Known Exoplanet Ever
item.description: Under 1 million years old, “Elias 2-24b” is now the youngest exoplanet ever observed, and it may force researchers to reevaluate theories about how planets are formed.

item.title: WIRED Business: A Prediction Market About the Past? Sure, Why Not!
item.description: As prediction markets surge in popularity, a new platform called Verifact Markets is pushing the concept even further, letting users trade on “disputed facts.”

item.title: The New Yorker: Year of the Horse
item.description: After a young tourist was killed in a Central Park carriage accident this summer, the City Council is considering whether to ban horse-drawn carriages forever.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Brigitte Chartrand Knows What You’ll Want to Wear Next
item.description: The Net-a-Porter buyer on Fashion Month, trusting her instincts, and packing 12 pairs of shoes.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: A Clinton Hill Townhouse Sets a Neighborhood Record for $9.4 Million
item.description: It’s another sign that the wobbly mansion market in the neighborhood (and nearby Fort Greene) is heating up.

item.title: Fox59: Woman killed in hit-and-run on Indy's west side
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS - The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department is investigating a fatal hit-and-run crash that occurred Sunday night. According to IMPD, a passerby reported seeing a person lying in the road unresponsive…
